title: Compactifications and refinements form a category
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Call a *compactification* of $f$ a triple $(\overline X,j,\bar f)$ of a scheme $\overline X$, an open immersion $j:X\to\overline X$ and a proper morphism $\bar f:\overline X\to Y$ with $\bar f\circ j=f$, and a *refinement* $u:(\overline X_1,j_1,\bar f_1)\to(\overline X_2,j_2,\bar f_2)$ a proper morphism of schemes $u:\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$ with $\bar f_2\circ u=\bar f_1$ and $u\circ j_1=j_2$. Then: (1) for every compactification $c=(\overline X,j,\bar f)$ the identity $\mathrm{id}_{\overline X}$ is a refinement $c\to c$; (2) for refinements $u:c_1\to c_2$ and $v:c_2\to c_3$ the composite $v\circ u:\overline X_1\to\overline X_3$ is a refinement $c_1\to c_3$. Consequently, since composition of morphisms of schemes is associative and unital, the compactifications of $f$ with the refinements as morphisms, identities $\mathrm{id}_{\overline X}$ and composition of morphisms of schemes, form a category [def-nagata-category] $\operatorname{Comp}(f)$. (The properness of $u$ is in fact automatic: $u$ is a morphism over $Y$ from a scheme proper over $Y$ to a scheme separated over $Y$.)
